Developing BlackThriveSS

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Use a fresh R session. Open the project and install maintainer tools as needed:

install.packages(c("roxygen2", "testthat", "pkgload", "rcmdcheck", "knitr", "rmarkdown"))
pkgload::load_all()
roxygen2::roxygenise()
testthat::test_local()

Never modify NAMESPACE or man/*.Rd by hand. Change the roxygen comments in R/ and regenerate them. Installation users need only the package’s Imports; the additional tools above are for maintainers.

Evidence and compatibility

  • Preserve existing release CSV bytes and identifiers. .gitattributes disables line-ending conversion for checksummed payloads.
  • Never replace an old release with a new extract under the same identifier. Preserve the 0.0.1 example view as a compatibility fixture.
  • Keep observed counts distinct from missing returns. Unknown ethnicity is not necessarily item non-response; the dashboard aggregates include vehicle-only searches that cannot be separated in this table.
  • A source-data change needs a new data release. A calculation or interpretation change needs a new method/release identity, a documented comparison and new validation. The current builder fingerprints source inputs; it deliberately refuses to overwrite them. Extend its identity scheme before releasing changed methods on identical inputs.
  • For a new chart algorithm, increment chart_version and preserve replay for existing supported versions, or fail explicitly. Do not silently reinterpret a saved specification.
  • A new chart attaches btg_figure_data and a btg_view built with .new_view() (schema 3), and registers its settings in .view_settings and its drawing call in .draw_view() in R/view.R. Settings are passed as arguments and never evaluated. The force ranking charts keep schema 2.
  • Groups keep the colours in btg_group_colours() in every chart; reference and de-emphasis colours come from btg_colours(). Do not assign colours by rank or value.
  • Statements written by btg_profile() must carry their qualification in the same sentence: the interval with the ratio, the coverage with a change, the allocation range with the unknown share. The briefing template in inst/rmarkdown/templates/briefing draws only from the profile and the exported chart functions.
  • Keep sampling intervals separate from assumption uncertainty. Do not infer discrimination from the descriptive ratio.

Tests

Use hand-calculated fixtures for mathematical correctness, corruption cases for data contracts, and saved-view round trips for compatibility. Test examples and vignettes offline. Do not access live police services in tests, examples or load hooks. Do not write to user files from examples; use tempfile() and clean up.

Dashboard parity is a separate developer check requiring the local public aggregate files and data.table. The packaged unit tests do not require that workspace, Shiny or any restricted dataset. dev/verify-dashboard.R verifies the four source-file hashes before comparing results.

Release workflow

  1. Update version and NEWS, regenerate help and run tests.
  2. Build with dev/build-release.R; this executes the vignette and creates the source archive plus installation ZIP.
  3. In a fresh process, test install.R into a new writable library. Exercise quickstart, package citation, validation, and the installed vignette.
  4. Run dev/check-release.R and review its complete log and every note. Associate all evidence with the archive SHA-256 in release.dcf.
  5. Run the CI matrix once a repository is established. Current R-devel and release checks are separate from the workstation’s installed R version.
  6. Complete the release gates in CRAN-READINESS.md and finalise cran-comments.md. Submission is a separate deliberate maintainer action.

The development bundle is a convenience installer; it is not part of the CRAN source package. No upload or public publication occurs in the build/check scripts.
